assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

evidence_rules: Preserve empirical observations, derived implications, inferred structure, mechanisms, reference theory, and unresolved questions as distinct layers.
Read-only sources: no source-data copies, database exports, reindexing, or large arrays. Persist only authored course artifacts, compact provenance, audits, and small clearly synthetic examples.
Cell3 uses ICRS columns [a b c], an intentional negative determinant, and half-open cells [-1/2,1/2)^3. Use x-O_K in affine reciprocal identities.
Use the mature locked geometry and exact source provenance. Historical and corrected numerical branches remain separately labeled; do not silently mix their constants.
Use M_cell=B^T B and R_cell=M_cell^-1; distinguish G_phase, G_eff, reciprocal bases, distance Q, Q_g, and Q_nu.
Gauge-carrier tuples use color-first C_3 direct-sum W_2. A weak-first view needs an explicit permutation.
Do not merge detector parity, A1 carry parity, projective signs, chirality, family labels, primitive lifts, or distinct dyadic and ternary recursions.
Declare nearest-integer half-ties and the corresponding residual interval consistently; the half-open cell ownership rule is a separate operation.
The detail-product identity needs explicit hypotheses on E beyond Q=I-E; retain the product of finite differences.
M19 contains mixed extension branches and is not a premise of M20 core closure. Reconstruct prerequisites from module requires, with the documented audit corrections.

Preserve mature-source claims and accepted integration dispositions separately. In the integration only compiler M03, M07, M08 have direct authority; these compiler labels are not automatically the mathematical-backbone module labels. Preserve the admitted global-form family Z1,Z2,Z3,Z6 and source-local uniqueness claims with explicit contracts.
Treat matching dimensions or graph labels as neither an intertwiner nor a proof. A missing proof body remains a source-reported status with a retrieval gap.

Physical CMB velocity is distinct from phase-transformed vectors; the testbench admitted speed is 369812.50200040644 m/s. The Galactic Center is a visual gauge; do not invent Solar or Galactic short-window dynamics.
A photon-equivalent model energy is not measured transferred energy, and phase is not force. Preserve signed events and the three independent plane-cost levels in the fourteen-row 2026-08-26 bundle.
Cell3 and galaxy-derived cells have separately typed units, metrics, handedness, scales, and normals. Recurrence is an explanatory target, not permission to merge definitions.
Every residual remains a primary coordinate. Transformations are reversible or accompanied by all removed components and reconstruction rules; no outlier deletion or significance-based erasure.

course_map.title: Scalar lifts and reconstructed shape
course_map.worked_example_capability: Trace the gravity-related scalar definitions to their source variables
course_map.assessment_target: Trace the gravity-related scalar definitions to their source variables

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Read the five gravity_scalar_lift formulas in S02 M19 and the missing-definition list in S03 AUD-009. Use y_ab=ln(A_ab/A_ref), etc., only as a declared classroom convention with positive areas and common A_ref. The displayed inverse algebra implies F=y_ac-y_bc and M=y_bc-y_ab; label these inferred coordinate formulas, not recovered archival definitions of F or M.

worked_example.task_and_answer: With y=(0,2,3), derived F=-1, M=3, G=9*0+8*2-11*3=-17. Substitution into the displayed inverse gives y_ab=(-17+8+9)/6=0, y_ac=(-17+2+27)/6=2, y_bc=(-17+8+27)/6=3. The inverse determinant is nonzero; the extra scalar organizes three coordinates, not a fourth independent shape variable.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: With y=(1,0,2), F=-2, M=1, G=-13. Recover (1,0,2) by the same three equations. A common log-area shift t leaves F,M unchanged and shifts G by6t, consistent with scale sensitivity. Integrating d ln Gamma2 also needs a reference/integration constant; do not invent it.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Logs of raw dimensional areas are incomplete without reference conventions. The scalar identities do not choose a force law. F/M/Gamma2 source definition bodies remain VERIFIED_NOT_LOADED; algebraic inference does not close that retrieval task.

course_map.title: Reciprocal inversion identities
course_map.worked_example_capability: Verify a small reciprocal reconstruction with its metric
course_map.assessment_target: Verify a small reciprocal reconstruction with its metric

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Supply a nonsingular basis B with length units, metric G=B^T B, integer address h and reciprocal q=B^-T h in inverse length units. Teach q dot q=h^T G^-1 h before Bragg inversion. Declare nonzero sine, positive wavelength/order, reciprocal scale sign, orientation, and the retained vector rho.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For B=diag(2,3,4) LU and h=(1,1,0), q=(1/2,1/3,0) LU^-1, q dot q=13/36 LU^-2, d=6/sqrt(13) LU and n_hat=(3,2,0)/sqrt(13). B^T q=h. In a separate synthetic Bragg example, m=2, wavelength=2 LU and sin(theta)=1/2 give d=4 LU. Angles30 and150 degrees both give that d and Gamma_B=ln(m/2)=0 with common length reference.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For h=(0,0,1), the same B gives q=(0,0,1/4), d=4 LU and n_hat=(0,0,1). For Bragg m=1, wavelength=3 LU, sin(theta)=1/2 gives d=3 LU and Gamma_B=ln(1/2). With h=(1,1,0), g=0 and rho=(1/10,-1/5,0), q_observed=(3/5,2/15,0); reconstruct q_observed=3^0 B^-T h+rho.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: sin(theta)=0 is excluded for positive m*wavelength; B singular is outside inverse formulas. In q=n_hat/d, d and n_hat must come from that same q. The perturbed q example has a different d from the unperturbed metric example. A reciprocal residual is retained, not rounded to zero. Adjacent scaling d_next=3d gives delta ln(d/L_ref)=ln3.

course_map.title: Geometry and proposed inertial response
course_map.worked_example_capability: Separate a directional kinematic calculation from a force law
course_map.assessment_target: Separate a directional kinematic calculation from a force law

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define directional velocity v dot n and acceleration a dot n with a unit normal and declared units. A kinematic projection describes motion. An inertial or force response requires a separately specified constitutive equation, mass parameters and initial/boundary conditions.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Take n=(0,0,1), v=(1,2,3) LU/T and a=(0,0,-2) LU/T^2. The projections are3 LU/T and -2 LU/T^2. Reversing n changes both signs; squared projections are invariant. These calculations supply no force coefficient.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For n=(3/5,4/5,0), v=(5,0,0) LU/T and a=(0,5,0) LU/T^2, projections are3 LU/T and4 LU/T^2. Check n dot n=1. If an explicitly proposed law supplies F_parallel=mu*a_parallel and mu=2 mass units, the conditional force is8 mass*LU/T^2; mark mu and the law as added premises.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A dimensionless scalar lift cannot be called a dimensional force without the missing conversion and law. Preserve orientation, signed components, perpendicular motion and any proposed constitutive residual.

course_map.title: Cycle counts and exceptional dimensions
course_map.worked_example_capability: Recompute finite counts before comparing named algebraic structures
course_map.assessment_target: Recompute finite counts before comparing named algebraic structures

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Build the graph before naming an algebra: vertices (i,j,k) with coordinates0,1,2 and one-coordinate nearest-neighbor edges. A connected graph has cycle dimension E-V+1; teach a spanning tree as V-1 independent edges. For the periodic graph add wrap edges with the same edge convention.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Open P3 cubed: V=27, E=3*2*3^2=54, cycle dimension54-27+1=28. Periodic graph: E=81 and cycle dimension55, adding27=24+3. Source M19 records55=52+3 with global windings. Direct counting verifies the numbers; a specified sector decomposition is an additional source construction.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For the two-dimensional open3x3 grid, V=9,E=12, cycle dimension4; periodic E=18 gives10. Given the source theorem dim H^2((Z3)^3,Z3)=6, count3^6=729 classes. State that this arithmetic uses, rather than proves, the cohomology dimension theorem.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: 52 matching the dimension of F4 does not specify an action. Keep the source SU(3) octonion-stabilizer and compact F4/Albert-algebra statements as source/theorem cards; finite graph enumeration is not their proof. E6/E7 real-form choices remain extensions.

course_map.title: An action needs more than a matching dimension
course_map.worked_example_capability: Identify the map needed to connect a cycle sector to an algebra action
course_map.assessment_target: Identify the map needed to connect a cycle sector to an algebra action

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: An action gives operators for each group element or Lie algebra generator and their relations. An intertwiner T obeys T rho(g)=sigma(g) T (or the generator version). Show an actual 2x2 example before requesting a missing map on the52-cycle sector. Domain, field, basis, bracket and normalization matter.

worked_example.task_and_answer: rho=diag(1,-1), sigma=diag(-1,1), T=[[0,1],[1,0]]. Both actions represent an involution, T is invertible and T rho=sigma T. Multiplying T by2 gives another intertwiner, so existence does not select a canonical one.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: rho=diag(1,-1), sigma=-I have dimension2 but traces0 and -2, so cannot be conjugate. A proposed identity T=I for the first pair fails: rho-sigma=diag(2,-2). Retain the nonzero defect matrix. For a proposed Lie action, the required defect is [R(X),R(Y)]-R([X,Y]) for each generating relation.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A table of equal dimensions does not give operators, preserve brackets or select a real form. List these as missing construction inputs for the specific F4 action, E6/E7 selection and physical cohomology coupling; do not invent a52x52 source action.

course_map.title: Comparing mechanism classes
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compare mechanisms by predictions, invariants, and required inputs
course_map.assessment_target: Compare mechanisms by predictions, invariants, and required inputs

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Compare explicit sufficient mechanism classes by shared observables, independent inputs, invariants and discriminating predictions. Use separately synthetic response laws as an exercise; do not present them as source laws or measured effects. Freeze parameters on one declared case before predicting another and retain the entire residual ledger.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Let a toy signed scalar response z be measured in U, and kinematic w=v dot n in LU/T. Hypothesis H1 predicts z=k*w, with k in U*T/LU; H2 predicts z=b*w^2, with b in U*T^2/LU^2. Set synthetic calibration w=1 LU/T,z=2U, giving k=2 and b=2 in their units. At w=-1, H1 predicts-2U while H2 predicts+2U; at w=2 they predict4U and8U. Reversal distinguishes odd from even response.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Synthetic check cases w=(-1,2), z=(-2,5) give H1 predictions(-2,4), residuals(0,1)U; H2 predictions(2,8), residuals(-4,-3)U. Neither replaces the input list with a score. A falsifiable extension proposes fixed k and odd reversal across new held orientations; failure is recorded as an orientation-resolved residual and motivates a specified extension.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Fitting a free parameter afresh on each test case removes the claimed forward test. A mechanism is sufficient only for its stated scope and inputs. Neither toy law yet accounts for mass reconstruction, binding or exceptional actions; list those unresolved bridges instead of asserting unification.

source_scope.scalar_lift: Displayed inverse identities are freshly checked under declared dimensionless log-area conventions. F=y_ac-y_bc and M=y_bc-y_ab are algebraically inferred here, not recovered archival definitions. Full source F/M/Gamma2 definitions and reference/integration constants remain VERIFIED_NOT_LOADED.
source_scope.reciprocal: Nonsingular B, explicit metric, positive lengths/order and nonzero sine are mandatory. Same/opposite-angle branches and the full signed vector rho are preserved. Bragg examples are synthetic and conditional; adjacent scale identity is a logarithmic ratio with common units.
source_scope.mechanism: Directional kinematics and scalar reconstruction do not by themselves specify a force law. Proposed response laws are explicitly synthetic and carry units, frozen calibration inputs, invariants, predictions and all signed residuals.
source_scope.exceptional: Graph cycle counts are independently enumerated. H^2 dimension6, SU(3) stabilizer and compact F4/Albert statements remain attributed source/theorem results, not newly proved by counts. The specific F4 action on52 cycles, E6/E7 real-form choices and physical cohomology coupling are unconstructed extensions needing explicit operators and intertwiners.
source_scope.boundary: M19 is a mixed D+E branch, not an M20/core-closure premise. Preserve constituent boundaries even when a stored branch endpoint is null.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Read the five gravity_scalar_lift formulas in S02 M19 and the missing-definition list in S03 AUD-009. Use y_ab=ln(A_ab/A_ref), etc., only as a declared classroom convention with positive areas and common A_ref. The displayed inverse algebra implies F=y_ac-y_bc and M=y_bc-y_ab; label these inferred coordinate formulas, not recovered archival definitions of F or M.

worked_example.task_and_answer: With y=(0,2,3), derived F=-1, M=3, G=9*0+8*2-11*3=-17. Substitution into the displayed inverse gives y_ab=(-17+8+9)/6=0, y_ac=(-17+2+27)/6=2, y_bc=(-17+8+27)/6=3. The inverse determinant is nonzero; the extra scalar organizes three coordinates, not a fourth independent shape variable.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: With y=(1,0,2), F=-2, M=1, G=-13. Recover (1,0,2) by the same three equations. A common log-area shift t leaves F,M unchanged and shifts G by6t, consistent with scale sensitivity. Integrating d ln Gamma2 also needs a reference/integration constant; do not invent it.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Logs of raw dimensional areas are incomplete without reference conventions. The scalar identities do not choose a force law. F/M/Gamma2 source definition bodies remain VERIFIED_NOT_LOADED; algebraic inference does not close that retrieval task.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Supply a nonsingular basis B with length units, metric G=B^T B, integer address h and reciprocal q=B^-T h in inverse length units. Teach q dot q=h^T G^-1 h before Bragg inversion. Declare nonzero sine, positive wavelength/order, reciprocal scale sign, orientation, and the retained vector rho.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For B=diag(2,3,4) LU and h=(1,1,0), q=(1/2,1/3,0) LU^-1, q dot q=13/36 LU^-2, d=6/sqrt(13) LU and n_hat=(3,2,0)/sqrt(13). B^T q=h. In a separate synthetic Bragg example, m=2, wavelength=2 LU and sin(theta)=1/2 give d=4 LU. Angles30 and150 degrees both give that d and Gamma_B=ln(m/2)=0 with common length reference.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For h=(0,0,1), the same B gives q=(0,0,1/4), d=4 LU and n_hat=(0,0,1). For Bragg m=1, wavelength=3 LU, sin(theta)=1/2 gives d=3 LU and Gamma_B=ln(1/2). With h=(1,1,0), g=0 and rho=(1/10,-1/5,0), q_observed=(3/5,2/15,0); reconstruct q_observed=3^0 B^-T h+rho.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: sin(theta)=0 is excluded for positive m*wavelength; B singular is outside inverse formulas. In q=n_hat/d, d and n_hat must come from that same q. The perturbed q example has a different d from the unperturbed metric example. A reciprocal residual is retained, not rounded to zero. Adjacent scaling d_next=3d gives delta ln(d/L_ref)=ln3.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Define directional velocity v dot n and acceleration a dot n with a unit normal and declared units. A kinematic projection describes motion. An inertial or force response requires a separately specified constitutive equation, mass parameters and initial/boundary conditions.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Take n=(0,0,1), v=(1,2,3) LU/T and a=(0,0,-2) LU/T^2. The projections are3 LU/T and -2 LU/T^2. Reversing n changes both signs; squared projections are invariant. These calculations supply no force coefficient.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For n=(3/5,4/5,0), v=(5,0,0) LU/T and a=(0,5,0) LU/T^2, projections are3 LU/T and4 LU/T^2. Check n dot n=1. If an explicitly proposed law supplies F_parallel=mu*a_parallel and mu=2 mass units, the conditional force is8 mass*LU/T^2; mark mu and the law as added premises.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A dimensionless scalar lift cannot be called a dimensional force without the missing conversion and law. Preserve orientation, signed components, perpendicular motion and any proposed constitutive residual.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Build the graph before naming an algebra: vertices (i,j,k) with coordinates0,1,2 and one-coordinate nearest-neighbor edges. A connected graph has cycle dimension E-V+1; teach a spanning tree as V-1 independent edges. For the periodic graph add wrap edges with the same edge convention.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Open P3 cubed: V=27, E=3*2*3^2=54, cycle dimension54-27+1=28. Periodic graph: E=81 and cycle dimension55, adding27=24+3. Source M19 records55=52+3 with global windings. Direct counting verifies the numbers; a specified sector decomposition is an additional source construction.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For the two-dimensional open3x3 grid, V=9,E=12, cycle dimension4; periodic E=18 gives10. Given the source theorem dim H^2((Z3)^3,Z3)=6, count3^6=729 classes. State that this arithmetic uses, rather than proves, the cohomology dimension theorem.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: 52 matching the dimension of F4 does not specify an action. Keep the source SU(3) octonion-stabilizer and compact F4/Albert-algebra statements as source/theorem cards; finite graph enumeration is not their proof. E6/E7 real-form choices remain extensions.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: An action gives operators for each group element or Lie algebra generator and their relations. An intertwiner T obeys T rho(g)=sigma(g) T (or the generator version). Show an actual 2x2 example before requesting a missing map on the52-cycle sector. Domain, field, basis, bracket and normalization matter.

worked_example.task_and_answer: rho=diag(1,-1), sigma=diag(-1,1), T=[[0,1],[1,0]]. Both actions represent an involution, T is invertible and T rho=sigma T. Multiplying T by2 gives another intertwiner, so existence does not select a canonical one.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: rho=diag(1,-1), sigma=-I have dimension2 but traces0 and -2, so cannot be conjugate. A proposed identity T=I for the first pair fails: rho-sigma=diag(2,-2). Retain the nonzero defect matrix. For a proposed Lie action, the required defect is [R(X),R(Y)]-R([X,Y]) for each generating relation.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A table of equal dimensions does not give operators, preserve brackets or select a real form. List these as missing construction inputs for the specific F4 action, E6/E7 selection and physical cohomology coupling; do not invent a52x52 source action.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Compare explicit sufficient mechanism classes by shared observables, independent inputs, invariants and discriminating predictions. Use separately synthetic response laws as an exercise; do not present them as source laws or measured effects. Freeze parameters on one declared case before predicting another and retain the entire residual ledger.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Let a toy signed scalar response z be measured in U, and kinematic w=v dot n in LU/T. Hypothesis H1 predicts z=k*w, with k in U*T/LU; H2 predicts z=b*w^2, with b in U*T^2/LU^2. Set synthetic calibration w=1 LU/T,z=2U, giving k=2 and b=2 in their units. At w=-1, H1 predicts-2U while H2 predicts+2U; at w=2 they predict4U and8U. Reversal distinguishes odd from even response.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Synthetic check cases w=(-1,2), z=(-2,5) give H1 predictions(-2,4), residuals(0,1)U; H2 predictions(2,8), residuals(-4,-3)U. Neither replaces the input list with a score. A falsifiable extension proposes fixed k and odd reversal across new held orientations; failure is recorded as an orientation-resolved residual and motivates a specified extension.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Fitting a free parameter afresh on each test case removes the claimed forward test. A mechanism is sufficient only for its stated scope and inputs. Neither toy law yet accounts for mass reconstruction, binding or exceptional actions; list those unresolved bridges instead of asserting unification.

lessons.bridge_to_teach: Build an atlas with separate columns for archived claims, freshly verified finite identities, conditional predictions, missing replay definitions and unconstructed extensions. Include pointers and complete dependency boundaries. M19 requires M07,M08,M10,M13,M18; it is not a premise of the M01–M18 core closure.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Enter M19 scalar inverse as a checked conditional algebraic reconstruction; F/M/Gamma2 bodies as AUD-009 missing definitions; reciprocal inversion as domain-limited identities with rho retained; graph counts as finite checks; cohomology dimension and exceptional carrier statements as source theorems. Enter specific F4 action, E6/E7 real-form selection and physical cohomology coupling as unconstructed extensions.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Assemble the practice reconstruction from lesson02, the H1/H2 signed residual table from lesson06 and its frozen-parameter reversal proposal. For every entry supply source pointer or synthetic definition, units, domain, retained information and the next missing map or test. Include a null-boundary check: a source endpoint cannot erase a constituent limitation (S03 AUD-010).

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Do not promote a source theorem card to a freshly replayed proof or a proposed mechanism to an observation. Keeping missing definitions visible is compatible with preserving the source frozen claim; report VERIFIED_NOT_LOADED without inventing a downgrade or a completed force law.
